core_obligations: Produce the open set W (proof lines 3966-3969): restriction of F to the Zariski site of U is a sheaf, so by the cited same-chapter-free result of Modules there is a Zariski open W which is the largest open subset on which the local section sigma vanishes, giving part (1).

Prove part (2) (proof lines 3970-3974): for phi : V -> U in S_etale, the image phi(V) is open and {V -> phi(V)} is an etale covering; if sigma|_V = 0 then the sheaf condition gives sigma|_{phi(V)} = 0, so vanishing over V is equivalent to phi(V) being contained in W.

Prove part (3) (proof lines 3975-3981): vanishing of (U, ubar, sigma) in the stalk at sbar means there is a morphism of etale neighbourhoods (V, vbar) -> (U, ubar) with sigma|_V = 0, and by part (2) this happens exactly when ubar lies in W.
proof_roadmap: Restrict F to the Zariski topology of U and use the standard openness of the zero locus of a section to get the largest such W.
For an etale map V -> U, apply the sheaf condition to the etale covering V -> phi(V) to move vanishing from V to its image, proving (2).
Translate vanishing in the stalk at a geometric point into vanishing on an etale neighbourhood and apply (2) to obtain (3).
difficulty_reason: The lemma locates the vanishing locus of a local section of an abelian sheaf on S_etale: it is the largest Zariski open subset W of U on which the section vanishes, it can be tested after pullback along any etale map V -> U, and membership of a geometric point of U in W is equivalent to vanishing of the corresponding element of the stalk (statement lines 3942-3963). The proof has three separate steps: existence of the largest W by restriction to the Zariski site (proof lines 3966-3969), the passage from vanishing over V to vanishing over its image using the sheaf condition for the etale covering {V -> phi(V)} (proof lines 3970-3974), and the translation of stalk vanishing into the existence of an etale neighbourhood on which the section vanishes, which then feeds back into the previous step (proof lines 3975-3981). The claim is H2: three short but genuinely different arguments.
